title: Traditional Armenian Calendar
intro: This traditional Armenian calendar counts the passage of days in an unchanging 365-day year. Unlike the modern Gregorian calendar, it does not insert a leap day.
summary: Twelve months of thirty days each, followed by five extra days.
epoch: Its epoch is 11 July AD 552 in the Julian calendar. That is the starting date used by this computational model.
history: It is called a wandering calendar because its 365-day years slowly move against the seasons. A tropical solar year is slightly longer than 365 days. Without a leap day, the calendar year slips gradually relative to the solar seasons.
limits: The model describes the traditional wandering year; later Armenian reforms and variations in historical local practice are separate subjects. The illustrations are schematic, not exact astronomical conversion charts.
